name: Disorder of Carbohydrate Absorption and Transport

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Carbohydrate Absorption and Transport Disorders

criteria.description: Chronic diarrhea and failure to thrive in infancy or early childhood
Abnormal carbohydrate absorption demonstrated by hydrogen breath test or disaccharidase enzyme assays
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding carbohydrate transporters or enzymes
Histological evidence of normal mucosa or mild villous atrophy without inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic diarrhea with failure to thrive plus abnormal carbohydrate absorption demonstrated by biochemical testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory; intestinal biopsy is supportive to exclude other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Osmotic diarrhea triggered by carbohydrate ingestion

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to carbohydrate malabsorption
searchTerms: abdominal fullness due to carb digestion issues
stools that float or look greasy
low or high salt levels from diarrhea
iron deficiency causing low blood counts
low blood sugar after eating carbs

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to vitamin deficiencies (e.g., peripheral neuropathy)
searchTerms: tingling or numbness due to vitamin deficiency

rare.symptomName: Failure of normal growth hormone response

searchTerms: metabolic acidosis with low blood pH

laboratory: Elevated breath hydrogen test after carbohydrate challenge
Reduced disaccharidase enzyme activity in intestinal biopsy
Electrolyte disturbances secondary to chronic diarrhea
imaging: Normal or mildly abnormal small bowel imaging
No structural abnormalities on abdominal ultrasound
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SLC5A1 (glucose transporter), SLC2A2 (GLUT2), or other carbohydrate transporter genes
other: Normal or mild villous atrophy on intestinal biopsy
Improvement of symptoms with carbohydrate-restricted diet

distinguishingFeatures: Specific lactose hydrogen breath test positivity
No genetic defects in carbohydrate transporters
Villous atrophy with inflammation on biopsy

redFlags: Failure to thrive despite nutritional interventions
Neurological deficits suggestive of vitamin deficiency
references: Orphanet: Disorder of carbohydrate absorption and transport - ORPHA:309001
Hoffman J, et al. Carbohydrate malabsorption disorders: clinical features and diagnosis. J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr. 2020.
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD). Carbohydrate Absorption Disorders. 2023.
